He played for [[Grand Rapids Christian High School]], where he was a [[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American in 2021]], and played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]], earning third-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] honors in 2023. He was selected with the 15th overall pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]] by the [[Atlanta Hawks]], where he played for two seasons. He also played for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] for one season. ==High school career== Kobe Bufkin was born in [[Grand Rapids, Michigan]] to Kimberly Camp and Michael Bufkin.{{cite web |title=2022-23 MEN'S BASKETBALL ROSTER: 2 Kobe Bufkin |url=https://mgoblue.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/kobe-bufkin/23520 |access-date=March 7, 2024 |website=[[MGoBlue.com]] |publisher=Board of Regents of the University of Michigan}} When he was five years old, he stated that he wanted to play for the [[Michigan Wolverines football]] team. and [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] as his final five on July 7. At the time Bufkin was {{height|ft=6|in=4}}, {{convert|175|lb}} and ranked 78th in the national class of 2021, 15th among [[shooting guard]]s and third in the state of Michigan by the [[247Sports]] composite rankings.{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/2420901734|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|2420901734}}|title=Grand Rapids' Kobe Bufkin puts Michigan State, Michigan in top 5; sets Friday decision date|work=[[The Detroit News]]|last=Hawkins |first= James|access-date=March 6, 2024|date=July 7, 2020|page=B.2|quote=}} Three days later he announced his verbal commitment to Michigan which pushed Michigan's 2021 class from the 5th-ranked class to the 3rd ranked.{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/2422261437|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|2422261437}}|title=Michigan basketball lands 4-star guard Kobe Bufkin|work=[[The Blade (Toledo, Ohio)|The Blade]]|last=Bastock |first=Ashley|access-date=March 6, 2024|date=July 10, 2020|page=|quote=}} By the time of his signing on November 11, 2020, he was the 63 ranked member of the class of 2021. 2021.{{cite web |last=Spencer |first=Jamal |title=Bufkin hopes to return to the court during the playoffs Bufkin was the state of Michigan's first McDonald's All-American since [[Deyonta Davis]] in [[2015 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2015]]. It was the fifth time that the University of Michigan had had multiple McDonald's All-American selections (first since [[Louis Bullock]], [[Robert Traylor]] and [[Albert White (basketball)|Albert White]] in [[1995 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|1995]]) and the third time that they had three or more.
